about: Hand-computed. madar-catalog `order`: the order a menu's categories are shown in, the POS's rule (madar-core `menu::categories`). `display_order` (missing or null = 0) ascending, then the name resolved for `locale` compared by Unicode code point, then `id`. `resolve` pins the name resolution (madar-core `menu::resolve`): the exact locale, its language, `en`, the base name; an empty or non-text translation is none. Each order case's `expected` is the categories' ids in the order shown.

resolve.name: english_before_the_base
resolve.why: no fr, no fr's language: en, ahead of the base name

resolve.name: base_when_nothing_matches
resolve.why: no ar and no en: the base name

resolve.name: empty_translation_falls_through
resolve.why: an empty ar is no ar: the base name

resolve.name: non_text_translation_is_ignored
resolve.why: ar is a number, not text: no ar

resolve.name: null_translations
resolve.why: no translations at all: the base name

categories.name: display_order_beats_the_alphabet
categories.why: 0, 1, 2 — the dashboard's drag order — not Breakfast, Coffee, Desserts

categories.name: a_tie_breaks_on_the_name
categories.why: Apple and Bread share 0: A < B; Zebra is 2 (the POS core's own test)

categories.name: missing_and_null_display_order_are_zero
categories.why: Tea (missing) and Juice (null) are both 0, ahead of Coffee's 1; between them J < T

categories.name: english_reader_ties_on_the_english_name
categories.why: both 0; en reads Coffee and Tea: C < T

categories.name: arabic_reader_ties_on_the_arabic_name
categories.why: the same two in ar read قهوة (U+0642 first) and شاي (U+0634 first): ش < ق, so Tea first — the tie follows the name the reader sees

categories.name: arabic_reader_untranslated_name_sorts_before_arabic
categories.why: in ar, Water has no ar and reads Water; W (U+0057) < ش (U+0634)

categories.name: position_still_beats_the_arabic_name
categories.why: in ar, شاي < قهوة, but Coffee is 0 and Tea is 1

categories.name: code_point_order_not_a_collation
categories.why: both 0: B (U+0042) < a (U+0061), so Banana before apple; a locale collation (Postgres en_US.UTF-8, JS localeCompare) puts apple first

categories.name: code_points_not_utf16_units
categories.why: both 0: Ｐ (U+FF30) < 🍕 (U+1F355); JavaScript's default string order compares UTF-16 units and puts the pizza (0xD83C) first

categories.name: equal_names_break_on_id
categories.why: two Drinks at 0: the id decides, a < b

categories.name: names_equal_only_in_arabic
categories.why: in ar both read مشروبات, so the id decides (a < b) — in en the names would (Drinks < Juices)

categories.name: a_whole_menu
categories.why: 0: Breakfast and Specials (missing = 0), B < S; 1: Cold drinks and Hot drinks, C < H; then 2 Sandwiches, 3 Desserts
